title: Catch the T-C-H
kidRule: Right after a short vowel sound, the /ch/ sound is usually spelled T-C-H, as in STRETCH. But look out for a few rule-breakers: MUCH, SUCH, RICH, and WHICH!
hint: We hear '/ch/' right after a short vowel sound, so a quiet letter sneaks in before the C-H. Which one?
reminder: Right after a short vowel sound, '/ch/' is spelled T-C-H, with a quiet T in front.

check.question: Why does STRETCH have a T before the C-H?
check.correctAnswer: Because the '/ch/' sound comes right after a short vowel sound!
distractors: Because every word that ends in C-H needs a T
Because the T makes the E say its name

words.def: The room where food is cooked.
words.sent: Something smells yummy in the kitchen.
words.story: The kitchen on a ship or an airplane has a special name: it is called a galley!
words.card: A *hen* in the *kitchen* is baking her own birthday cake!

words.def: To make something longer by pulling it, or to reach out your body as far as it goes.
words.sent: Cats stretch their legs after a long nap.
words.story: A chameleon can stretch its sticky tongue out farther than the length of its whole body!
words.card: My sec*ret* trick is to *stretch* like a noodle every morning!

words.def: One loop of thread made with a needle.
words.sent: Grandma sewed one more stitch on my teddy bear.
words.story: A little bird called the tailorbird sews leaves together with spider silk to make its nest!
words.card: One *stitch* fixed the *itch*y hole in my sock!

words.def: To rub your skin with your fingernails, or to make a thin mark with something sharp.
words.sent: Cats scratch trees to keep their claws sharp.
words.story: When a cat claws at a tree, it also leaves behind a smell from its paws that says 'I was here!'
words.card: The *rat* had to *scratch* his ear with a tiny fork!

words.def: A tall jug with a handle and a spout for pouring drinks.
words.sent: Mom poured lemonade from a big glass pitcher.
words.story: There is a plant called the pitcher plant. Its leaves are shaped like little jugs, and bugs that fall in become its dinner!
words.card: The lemonade *pitcher* fell into a *pit* of marshmallows!

words.def: A thick red tomato sauce for fries and burgers.
words.sent: I squeezed ketchup all over my fries.
words.story: Long ago, this sauce had no tomatoes in it at all. It was made from things like fish or mushrooms!
words.card: The *ketchup* shot *up* and landed on the ceiling fan!

words.def: A long stick that fits under your arm to help you move around when your leg is hurt.
words.sent: He used a crutch after he hurt his ankle.
words.story: People have used these walking helpers for thousands of years. A very old carving from Egypt shows a person leaning on one!
words.card: The snowman used a *cru*nchy carrot as a *crutch*!

words.def: A small tool with a short handle and a sharp blade for chopping wood.
words.sent: The camper used a hatchet to split wood for the fire.
words.story: When people say they will 'bury the hatchet', they mean they are going to stop arguing and be friends again!
words.card: The beaver traded his *hatchet* for a fancy *hat*!

words.def: A bag with a long strap that you wear over your shoulder, often used for carrying books.
words.sent: She packed her books and an apple into her satchel.
words.story: Mail carriers in the United States carry letters in a satchel. A full one can weigh as much as 35 pounds!
words.card: The cat *sat* inside my *satchel* and ate my homework!

words.def: To send someone or something off quickly to a place.
words.sent: The station will dispatch a fire truck right away.
words.story: Long before phones, people would dispatch messages by pigeon. Homing pigeons can find their way home from hundreds of miles away!
words.card: Quick, *dispatch* a pirate to sew a *patch* on my teddy bear!
